issues.title: Missing boundedness for the enclosing-radius construction

failure_location.quote: Then there exists an $x_0\in\R^n$ (which we assume without loss of generality to be the origin) such that $\Omega\subset B_r(x_0)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that an enclosing center x_0 exists at the radius r for every domain admitted by the old setup. The old paper actually assumes only that Omega is Lipschitz, which permits unbounded domains such as a half-plane. For such a domain the set of finite enclosing radii is empty, so r is not finite, no asserted enclosing ball exists, and the subsequent requirements T>4r and the finite reconstruction domain cannot be formed.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-time admissible reconstruction region and the Radon-domain construction are justified only for bounded domains, not for every Lipschitz domain allowed by the old introductory wording.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the standing setup, or at least the enclosing-radius and Radon reconstruction construction, to bounded Lipschitz domains. Under that hypothesis, state that the finite minimal enclosing radius is attained, translate an attaining center to the origin, and retain the conditions T>4r and the associated reconstruction regions only within this bounded-domain scope.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained, source-supported repair and requires no new proof architecture, but it excludes the natural and broad class of unbounded Lipschitz domains admitted by the old setup. The bounded-domain construction remains recognizably the same, so the model-class loss is limited rather than major, making the issue moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Undefined zeroth-order Gaussian constant
issues.primary_affected_tag: lemma: reguderis relation of any two

failure_location.tag: lemma: reguderis relation of any two

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $s> 0$ and $p$ be a non-negative integer with $p\leq s$.

issues.failure_explanation: The quantified range includes p=0, while the formula for C_p and the proof's maximum value are undefined there. Directly evaluating the zeroth-order multiplier gives supremum 1, so the omitted endpoint case is C_0=1.
dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: thm: reguderis error estimate for Gaussian
issues.overall_effect: The lemma and the later theorem that imports C_p are not well-defined at p=0. Positive derivative orders, including the paper's third-derivative application, are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define C_0=1 and retain C_p=(2e/p)^(-p/2) for p>=1. Split the proof at p=0, using sup_xi exp(-alpha xi^2)=1 there, and use this piecewise definition of C_p in the dependent theorem.
issues.why_classification: The endpoint requires a genuine separate calculation, so it is not merely typographical. That calculation is immediate and local, preserves the lemma and dependent theorem for every stated derivative order with the same rate, and requires no new lemma or substantive weakening.

issues.title: Missing Gaussian regularization-parameter choice
issues.primary_affected_tag: thm: reguderis error estimate for Gaussian

failure_location.tag: thm: reguderis error estimate for Gaussian

diagnostic_evidence.tag: lemma: reguderis relation of any two
lemma: reguderis relation of exact and regu

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies s, p, delta, g, and g_delta but leaves alpha unbound. Its proof invokes two lemmas whose hypotheses fix alpha=delta^{2/s}. For p<s, taking g_delta=g and a fixed nonzero alpha leaves a positive regularization bias for suitable g as delta tends to zero, while the claimed right-hand side tends to zero.
issues.overall_effect: The stated rate is supported only for the balanced regularization parameter, not for a free or arbitrary alpha.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the parameter choice alpha=delta^(2/s) to the theorem's hypotheses before the estimate. With that choice, the stated triangle-inequality proof applies the two cited lemmas directly; the surrounding discussion should identify the estimate as holding for this balanced parameter.
issues.why_classification: The unbound parameter is a genuine dependency defect because the proof cannot invoke its lemmas without the missing choice. Nevertheless, both cited lemmas and the following prose uniquely supply the same choice, so the repair is short and routine and preserves the intended theorem, rate, domain, and proof without meaningful loss.

issues.title: Finite-tau Radon reconstruction stated as exact
issues.failure_explanation: The boundary waves defining g depend on tau. Equation eq: recoequ Radon proves that the corresponding boundary integral converges to the Radon transform as tau tends to infinity, and lemma:approx Radon supplies a finite-tau approximation error. It does not imply equality for the finite tau used in the numerical construction.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-tau estimator remains a justified approximation, but it is not an exact Radon value; finite-tau smoothing and reconstruction blur must be retained in its interpretation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write g as g_tau if necessary and replace the finite-tau equality by R(q)=lim_{tau to infinity} partial_epsilon^3 g_tau(0). For finite tau, state the approximation and the corresponding error supplied by the Radon approximation lemma (including any cutoff contribution), and interpret the regularized numerical output as a finite-tau smoothed estimator rather than an exact Radon value.
issues.why_classification: The existing lemma gives a contained quantitative repair and the estimator, convergence, and reconstruction architecture all survive. However, replacing exact finite-tau recovery by an approximation with nonzero smoothing error is a meaningful but limited weakening of the recorded conclusion, so the issue exceeds minor severity while avoiding global reconstruction or major mathematical loss.
